synopsis: 30 CFR 77.410 is in force for US surface coal operations and requires specified mobile equipment—including loaders, forklifts, tractors, graders and trucks—to have a reverse alarm or discriminating detection [f2766, f2232, f15510]. Permitted detection technologies include infrared, ultrasonic, radar or another effective device; lidar is not named and should not be described as approved, although it could fall under the latter category [f2084, f2235, f15511]. The sensing area must give an endangered person adequate time to escape, but the rule specifies no fixed range in metres or speed [f2233, f2622, f2443]. The corpus also identifies internal audible and visual warnings, external audible warnings, and a requirement that alarms be audible above surrounding noise [f2234, f2445]. Crucially for automatic-braking validation planning, this rule does not require automatic braking [f2236, f2769].

relations.note: Both state the equipment obligation and reverse-alarm or discriminating-detection alternatives.
Both identify accepted detection technologies and the escape-sized sensing area.
Both caution that unnamed lidar should not be described as approved.
Both require reverse alarms or specified discriminating detection in surface coal operations.
Both state that automatic braking is not required.
Both require adequate escape time through the detection sensing area.
Both require escape-enabling sensing coverage; the latter clarifies absence of a metre-based range.
Both require a sensing area sufficient for endangered persons to escape.
The chapter clarifies that the glossary's escape-area requirement has no specified range in metres.
Adds internal and external warning requirements to the glossary's escape-area description.
Both specify internal audible and visual warnings plus external audible warnings.
Adds the requirement that audible alarms exceed surrounding noise.
Adds rearward person-or-object scope and absence of a fixed speed.
Clarifies that the alarm-or-detection obligation does not extend to automatic braking.
